title: Your first script
prompt:
Write a script `hello.sh` in Mira’s home directory that prints exactly this line:

```
Hello from TuxPixel
```

It must start with a shebang line for Bash and be executable, so that Mira can run it as `./hello.sh`. Use `nano hello.sh` (save with Ctrl+O, Enter, leave with Ctrl+X), or `cat > hello.sh` and Ctrl+D.
hints: The first line, the shebang, names the interpreter: `#!/bin/bash`.
The second line can be `echo "Hello from TuxPixel"`.
`chmod +x hello.sh` makes it executable; then run `./hello.sh`.
solution:
cat > hello.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
echo "Hello from TuxPixel"
EOF
chmod +x hello.sh
check:
if [ ! -e hello.sh ]; then no "There is no hello.sh yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "hello.sh exists."
if head -n 1 hello.sh | grep -Eq '^#! ?(/usr)?/bin/(env )?(ba)?sh'; then ok "It starts with a shebang line."; else no "Its first line isn’t a shebang such as #!/bin/bash."; fi
if runuser -u mira -- test -x hello.sh; then ok "Mira may execute it."; else no "It isn’t executable. Use chmod."; exit 1; fi
out=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira USER=mira LOGNAME=mira PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=en_US.UTF-8 timeout 5 bash -c 'cd ~ && ./hello.sh' < /dev/null 2>&1)
if [ "$out" = 'Hello from TuxPixel' ]; then ok "./hello.sh prints “Hello from TuxPixel”."; else no "./hello.sh prints “$out”."; fi

title: Welcome, whoever you are
prompt:
Write an executable Bash script `welcome.sh` in Mira’s home directory that greets the name given as its first argument:

```
$ ./welcome.sh Ada
Welcome, Ada!
```

Without an argument it must print a line that starts with `Usage:` (for example `Usage: welcome.sh NAME`) and exit with the status 1.
hints: Inside a script, `$1` is the first argument and `exit 1` ends the script with the status 1.
`if [ -z "$1" ]; then … fi` runs its commands when `$1` is empty.
Test it with `./welcome.sh Ada`, `./welcome.sh` and `echo $?`, which shows the last exit status.
solution:
cat > welcome.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
if [ -z "$1" ]; then
  echo "Usage: welcome.sh NAME"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Welcome, $1!"
EOF
chmod +x welcome.sh
check:
if [ ! -e welcome.sh ]; then no "There is no welcome.sh yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "welcome.sh exists."
if runuser -u mira -- test -x welcome.sh; then ok "It is executable."; else no "It isn’t executable. Use chmod."; exit 1; fi
out=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira USER=mira LOGNAME=mira PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=en_US.UTF-8 timeout 5 bash -c 'cd ~ && ./welcome.sh Ada' < /dev/null 2>&1)
if [ "$out" = 'Welcome, Ada!' ]; then ok "./welcome.sh Ada prints “Welcome, Ada!”."; else no "./welcome.sh Ada prints “$out”, not “Welcome, Ada!”."; fi
out=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira USER=mira LOGNAME=mira PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=en_US.UTF-8 timeout 5 bash -c 'cd ~ && ./welcome.sh Jonas' < /dev/null 2>&1)
if [ "$out" = 'Welcome, Jonas!' ]; then ok "It works for other names too."; else no "./welcome.sh Jonas prints “$out”. Use the argument, don’t type the name."; fi
out=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira USER=mira LOGNAME=mira PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=en_US.UTF-8 timeout 5 bash -c 'cd ~ && ./welcome.sh' < /dev/null 2>&1); st=$?
if printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 1 | grep -q '^Usage:'; then ok "Without an argument it prints a usage line."; else no "Without an argument it prints “$out”, not a line starting with Usage:."; fi
if [ "$st" = 1 ]; then ok "Without an argument it exits with the status 1."; else no "Without an argument it exits with the status $st, not 1."; fi

title: Back up the sprites with a loop
prompt:
Write an executable Bash script `backup.sh` in Mira’s home directory that:

1. creates the folder `~/backup` if it doesn’t exist yet,
2. copies each `.png` file from `~/art` into it with a `for` loop,
3. and prints the name of every file it copies.

Run it twice: the second run must work too.
hints: `mkdir -p ~/backup` creates the folder, and does nothing (without an error) when it already exists.
`for f in ~/art/*.png; do … done` runs the body once for each PNG file, with its path in `$f`.
solution:
cat > backup.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
mkdir -p ~/backup
for f in ~/art/*.png; do
  cp "$f" ~/backup/
  echo "$f"
done
EOF
chmod +x backup.sh
check:
if [ ! -e backup.sh ]; then no "There is no backup.sh yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "backup.sh exists."
if runuser -u mira -- test -x backup.sh; then ok "It is executable."; else no "It isn’t executable. Use chmod."; exit 1; fi
if grep -Eq '^\s*for\b' backup.sh; then ok "It uses a for loop."; else no "It doesn’t use a for loop."; fi
rm -rf backup
out=$(runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira USER=mira LOGNAME=mira PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=en_US.UTF-8 timeout 5 bash -c 'cd ~ && ./backup.sh' < /dev/null 2>&1); st=$?
if [ "$st" = 0 ] && [ "$(ls backup 2> /dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')" = 'bat.png hero.png slime.png ' ]; then ok "Run on a clean home, it copies the three PNG files, and only those."
else no "Run on a clean home, ~/backup holds “$(ls backup 2> /dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')” (exit status $st), not the three PNG files."; fi
if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q hero.png && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q slime.png && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q bat.png; then ok "It prints the name of each file it copies."; else no "It doesn’t print the name of each file it copies."; fi
runuser -u mira -- env -i HOME=/home/mira USER=mira LOGNAME=mira PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=en_US.UTF-8 timeout 5 bash -c 'cd ~ && ./backup.sh' < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1; st=$?
if [ "$st" = 0 ]; then ok "A second run works too."; else no "A second run fails with the status $st. Does mkdir fail when ~/backup exists?"; fi
